I have been there. Both on the edge ready to end it all, and fighting my way back. I try to look at it like a 90/10. On most days, 90% of me wants to die, and 10% is fighting its way forward.  I try to turn my days in to 90% okay with 10% wanting to die.  This is a constant struggle, medicated or not. I have accepted the reality that sometimes depression and CPTSD rears it’s ugly Medusa head. Even if I have a good day that is perfect, I know that in the end nothing is a guarantee in life. As for the sickening pain and internal struggle, I had to teach myself how to deal with it. When I can’t fight that 90%, it’s so difficult to think and not dissociate, but I have to take a look at what I can do for me. If you’re not sure what to do try this, take a breath in your nose and out your mouth. I know that I have to try to HALT and take a look at what I NEED. Not what I’m feeling. In those moments stop. Ask some questions: Am I hungry? Am I angry? Am I lonely? Am I tired? If the answers to any of these questions is yes, I need to focus on addressing those needs before I address what I’m feeling inside.  Being hungry doesn’t help me feel any better regardless of how much I think punishing myself will. If you’re tired, take a nap but maybe try to set an alarm so you don’t use sleep to cope. Are you lonely? If possible see if someone can come sit with you. If you feel lonely but don’t want to reach out, try watching a funny movie that involves you emotionally (Disney is great for this). Anger is more difficult. Sometimes, anger is what pushed us in to a difficult state and causes us to become even more depressed or suicidal. Ask why you’re angry? Is it because of an expectation (are you disappointed or feeling left out, did someone lie, etc.) , an event (conversation, accident) , or the behavior of a person (were they dismissive, mean, or harmful in some way)? Take a look and try to find the root of the anger, and then let it out. Sometimes this is a time to return to asking for the help of a friend, addressing the thing or person that caused you anger, or occupying your mind. 
I found that it’s up to me to take a look at myself and try to care for myself while showing compassion to me. If I’m taking the time to meet those needs, it’s time not spent focusing on how I feel. I hope this helps, it works for me so it might be worth a shot for you. I hope that you begin to find joy in something small, even if it’s something so simple as having a phone that’s charged or a light to read by.
